subject: 20280816 VentureMeds inference ops & SLO qualification
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@venturemeds.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@venturemeds.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Aug 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: VentureMeds discovery — throughput constraints, latency targets, next steps

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks for the call today — good overview of how VentureMeds intends to use summarization and entity extraction across claims ingestion and provider notes. To make sure we captured the important bits, quick recap below and proposed next steps.

Key pain points / goals we heard:
- High sustained ingest during business hours (batch ingestion + near-real-time corrections). Peak bursts ~500–800 requests per second (QPS) for short summarization requests; baseline steady-state ~120 QPS.
- Latency requirement for interactive UI flows: p95 <= 150ms for single-turn summarization (average prompt ~150 tokens, expected response ~100 tokens).
- Background batch jobs (overnight) should be cheap and high-throughput; latency for those can be relaxed to seconds.
- Strong data residency requirement (US), and audit/logging for PHI workflows — likely Private or Dedicated deployment with customer-managed networking.

Model / accuracy notes you shared:
- You prefer open models with fine-tuning options; priority is factuality on clinical snippets and hallucination reduction.
- Typical prompt sizes today are 400–800 tokens when we include context windows; the UI trims context but we should plan for 1k context in provisioning.

Initial topology & ops constraints (items to validate):
- Dedicated GPU pool for production inference (predictable latency, isolation).
- Autoscaling must cover 2x burst over baseline without cold-start penalties; consider burst capacity for marketing/regulatory spikes.
- KV/prefix caching for repeated patient-context tokens to reduce per-token load.
- Token retention policy, encryption, and audit logs (we'll send SOC2 evidence in a separate attachment).

Proposed next steps
1) You to share a representative sample of request/response pairs (anonymized) + traffic histogram (attach CSV).
2) We run an initial capacity estimate and provide an SLA sketch (attached: sla-proposal-v1.pdf).
3) Schedule a 90-minute technical workshop (deep dive: model variants, quantization profiles, integration points) — suggested windows next Wed/Thu.

Attachments: venturemeds-sample-traffic.csv (please anonymize), sla-proposal-v1.pdf

If that looks right, I’ll assemble a short mutual action plan and a topology sketch for the workshop.

Best,
Monica Patel

Subject: Re: Recap: VentureMeds discovery — throughput constraints, latency targets, next steps

Thanks Monica — this is a great summary and aligns with our notes. A couple quick clarifications before the workshop:

- The 500–800 bursts are 95th percentile concurrent requests during peak claims intake windows; they’re short-lived (1–5 minutes) but frequent (a few times per hour).
- Token distribution: ~60% of requests are small (<200 tokens total), 30% are medium (200–800), and ~10% are long (>800). We can provide a daily distribution CSV.
- We need to keep request logs for 90 days for troubleshooting; logs must be encrypted and accessible via an audit API.

We’ll attach the anonymized sample traffic and a Redis-like key pattern that drives our context cache. Also fine to aim for dedicated capacity — curious about cost delta between dedicated and private.

Sam

Subject: Re: Recap: VentureMeds discovery — throughput constraints, latency targets, next steps

Sam — thanks for the clarifications; attaching a short technical sketch and a proposal for the workshop agenda. High-level technical readout below so the engineering folks have something concrete to react to ahead of the workshop.

Technical deep-dive (summary)
- Target SLOs (interactive flows): p50 <= 30–40ms, p95 <= 110–150ms for typical short requests (<= 512 context tokens). For long context (~1k tokens) expect p95 to increase ~1.6x; we can bound this with model selection and KV cache.
- Throughput provisioning: for baseline 120 QPS + 2x buffer + peak burst tolerance (800 QPS), recommend a Dedicated pool sized for ~600 steady QPS with autoscale headroom of GPU-backed burst nodes (stateless routing + warm pool) to handle spikes.
- Model choices: open LLM family (we recommend evaluating two variants: a 13B tuned variant for interactive and a 70B quantized variant for higher-fidelity batch work). Both should be tested with int8/4 quantization profiles we can propose.
- Batching / latency tradeoffs: continuous batching helps cost but increases p95. For interactive SLOs, we recommend a small max batch (4–8) with latency-first kernel selection; for background batch jobs, use larger batch sizes (32–128) and lower precision to reduce cost.
- KV/prefix caching: keep per-patient context cached (hot keys) in memory on inference nodes; this should cut per-request compute by ~30–60% depending on repetition.
- Topology sketch: Private control plane (for audit/KMS), Dedicated inference pool (GPU instances with warm pool), optional cloud-provider-managed object-store for prompts, and an ops-side audit API. (See attachment: inference-topology-sketch.png.)

Estimated runbook items for the workshop
1) Confirm authorization flows and KMS key access pattern (who needs crypto-unseal rights).
2) Evaluate a 48-hour load replay using the sample traffic to validate p95 under warm cache.
3) Agree on retention and redaction plan for logs (90-day encrypted retention + API access).
4) Identify a pilot customer slice (50k monthly active users) to scope cost and SLA.

I added a short cost/latency table in the topology sketch and the HubSpot deal link is below so we can track the MAP items. If this looks right I’ll send a Doodle to lock the 90-minute workshop — suggested: Thu 23rd or Fri 24th (morning PT).

Attachments: inference-topology-sketch.png
Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/VMED-2028-082

Looping in a couple of engineering notes from our side before the workshop:

- Warm pool sizing: based on the sample traffic, we’ll preliminarily propose a warm pool of 8–12 H100-backed nodes for the 600 QPS steady recommendation; we’ll run a bench matrix with quantized 70B vs tuned 13B to validate memory footprint and KV-cache hit behavior.
- Autoscale behavior: we need an agreed cold-start policy for burst nodes; my recommendation is fast warm-up using paused containers and a short-lived pre-warm window (60–120s) triggered by traffic anomalies.
- Integration checklist: auth headers (JWT), streaming vs non-streaming endpoints, retry/circuit-breaker guidance, and schema for the audit log (we’ll provide a sample JSON schema in the workshop).

Proposed workshop slots: Thu 23 Aug 09:00–10:30 PT or Fri 24 Aug 11:00–12:30 PT — which works best for your eng team?

Rishi
